requirement_catalog.summary: Each accepted scalar beat carries one IEEE-754 binary16 bit pattern and remains native-AWQ W4A16 compatible.
Finite binary16 values, including subnormals, decode exactly to signed Q40.24.
Q24 results convert to binary16 with round-to-nearest, ties-to-even, signed-zero policy, and finite-overflow saturation.
NaN or infinity marks the affected result or transaction invalid and returns positive zero without saturation.
State advances only on ready-valid handshakes and output data, index, last, and status remain stable under backpressure.
Active-low asynchronous reset and active-high synchronous clear abort and clear the current transaction.
Starts are accepted only for legal nonzero counts; RMSNorm requires exactly HIDDEN_SIZE.
Residual addition exactly sums projection and residual Q24 values before one binary16 rounding boundary.
RMSNorm uses the frozen two-pass Q24/Q48 equation, 92-bit workspace, epsilon, and 46-cycle integer square root.
SiLU/gate uses the frozen Q0.24 rational sigmoid and exact wide gate product before one Q24 and one binary16 rounding boundary.
Default dimensions are hidden size 896 and MLP intermediate size 4864 while core bounds remain parameterized.
The declared cycle boundaries are one cycle for residual-add and SiLU/gate and 46 post-load square-root cycles for RMSNorm.
ACE-3 arithmetic is first-party RTL; only the enumerated ACE-2 control, protocol, dataflow, and verification structures are re-expressed.
The fixed projection cluster composes unchanged native asymmetric G128 AWQ engines as Q 896x896, K 896x128, and V 896x128 lanes.
RoPE accepts every one of 14 query heads and two key heads, pairs dimensions p and p+32 for 64-dimensional heads, and carries the 32768-position Qwen2.5 coefficient index.
Each Qwen2.5 half-split rotation rounds both binary16 products before the binary16 sum, returns positive zero for non-finite operands, and saturates finite overflow.
The one-entry RoPE ready-valid stage retains data, metadata, and status under backpressure; reset and clear abort its pending output.
Separate FP16 K and V arrays plus validity metadata are indexed in cache-slot, position, K/V-head, dimension order with defaults 2x128x2x64.
Accepted writes update exactly one K/V index; reads return a retained hit or positive-zero miss; overwrites replace one entry and simultaneous same-address access is write-through.
Reset and clear invalidate every cache entry and abort a pending response without claiming reset of K/V SRAM data bits.
The independent bit-level oracle and generated streams are bound to the fixed official checkpoint and cross-checked in Icarus and Verilator with tamper rejection.
This milestone stops at QKV projection geometry, pairwise RoPE, and indexed FP16 K/V storage; all downstream model execution and physical implementation claims remain excluded.
The projection wrapper, RoPE pair core, and K/V cache are first-party ACE-3 RTL with explicit dependencies on accepted ACE-3 arithmetic and projection modules.
The attention cores implement 14 query heads, two K/V heads, 64-element heads, floor(query_head/7) GQA mapping, and key_position <= query_position causal eligibility.
Score accumulation decodes finite FP16 Q/K exactly to Q24, accumulates 64 Q48 products, applies the exact 1/8 scale with RNE, and converts once to FP16.
Causal softmax uses Q24 max subtraction, the frozen 17-point Q0.24 exponential interpolation, exact denominator accumulation, and RNE normalization.
Value composition accumulates required FP16 probability/V products exactly in Q48 and converts the final Q24 result once to FP16.
Reset and clear abort active work, outputs remain stable under backpressure, and invalid or unknown configuration and payload metadata cannot be accepted.
Hash-authenticated official-checkpoint-derived and directed vectors are independently recomputed and compared in Icarus four-state and Verilator two-state simulation with tamper rejection.
The attention claim stops at standalone score, causal softmax, and value-composition cores and excludes decoder, model, physical-implementation, and performance claims.
The three attention cores are first-party ACE-3 RTL bound to the fixed official model identity and the accepted FP16 conversion helpers.

coverage_obligations: Icarus executes Q 896x896, K 896x128, and V 896x128 geometry while Verilator lints the same fixed cluster.
Both dynamic simulators compare 512 RoPE cases bit-for-bit and require all 14 query heads, both key heads, metadata retention, and output backpressure stability.

Both dynamic simulators check indexed K/V writes and reads, both value heads, misses, overwrite, slot/position/head/dimension isolation, cache-output stalls, reset invalidation, and clear invalidation.
Icarus additionally checks same-address write-through and four-state X/Z non-acceptance for idle RoPE and cache inputs.
The validator rejects a modified rope_cases.hex by serialized SHA256 before simulation.
The validator independently recomputes 20 score cases, 20 softmax rows with 140 probabilities, and 20 value-composition cases spanning every query head and both GQA K/V groups.

Official-derived operands are deterministic selections from hash-authenticated layer-0 q_proj FP16 scales, not captured runtime Q/K/V activations; directed cases cover masks, misses, invalids, saturation, cancellation, and upstream row errors.
Both simulators compare every retained numerical result and status and check reset, clear, output backpressure, causal masking, cache-miss propagation, and invalid GQA configuration rejection.
Icarus additionally requires six bounded X/Z non-acceptance checks; Verilator repeats the legal arithmetic and protocol surface as a two-state build and simulation.
A modified attention_score_terms.hex must fail serialized SHA256 authentication before simulation.
